finish.summary: I built a seed-starting tray with four hex cells, each holding a draining bin. The cells sit in a tight diamond at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) and (1,-1). Each one has a half-depth drained bin (hex-bin-half-drain) filled with soil and planted with a seedling, so you can see what the tray is for. I closed the open outer faces with solid end caps and bolted the joints between cells. The finished build is 22 parts, about 1777 g of filament and roughly 2594 minutes to print. The final check found no rule issues, the parts don't collide, and there are no warnings about the soil or plants. Nothing here checks whether the bins hold up to water or soil over time; that depends on the filament you print in.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
